scope: Exploratory PCI QEMU HVF runs; not live UTM or physical Pi acceptance.

trial.change: Use the pinned upstream DocPrintPartial for each existing output chunk. The initial trial was reverted while investigating memory; a later build reinstates the same source change.
trial.debug_demo: Original DebugDemo printed for over five seconds, responded to Ctrl-Alt-C, and the terminal returned 42 with zstatus failed=0.
trial.document_flag_probe: Passed: the peer ran after Print only when DOCF_DONT_SWAP_OUT was clear.
trial.user_text: Functional startup, input, recovery and repeated close checks passed, but the no-growth check saw data bytes increase by 592 across two further cycles while code bytes and allocation count stayed constant.

baseline_recheck.result: The same functional checks passed, but the no-growth check also failed, with data bytes increasing by 96 and code bytes and allocation count unchanged. This establishes that the baseline already fails this check; it does not establish the cause of either increase.

diagnostic_rerun.change: Temporary zstatus per-task heap totals only; removed after the run.
diagnostic_rerun.result: The initial cycle passed, but UserTextLongChecks returned 1 on the next cycle because ZcTaskWaitTimeout did not complete within its 15-second limit. The run ended before a second heap snapshot, so allocation ownership was not determined.

ownership_comparison.change: Temporary zstatus per-task heap totals and an exploratory test variant. The full long-input check ran once; the following two terminal cycles omitted it and included extra zstatus snapshots. Both temporary changes were removed.
ownership_comparison.result: Functional checks passed, but whole-system data usage changed from 31411504 to 31411152 to 31411568 bytes. The allocation count stayed 151289 and the global data heap stayed at 23007232 bytes. The live AutoComplete task changed from 33568 to 33232 to 33680 bytes; task 2 changed by -16 and task 10 by -32 bytes. AutoComplete is a background task, so whole-system growth alone does not establish a terminal teardown leak. These snapshots also do not prove terminal cleanup is correct.
ownership_comparison.guest_log_note: The original guest log was subsequently overwritten by a later run; the runner log above is retained.

partial_output_recheck.debug_demo: Original DebugDemo printed 163 dots, and serial command evaluation returned 42 after Ctrl-Alt-C. A later repeat exposed that the graphical terminal had actually been stopped, so this was not graphical recovery. Ctrl-Alt-D is not verified.
partial_output_recheck.document_flags: Focused output test passed with and without DOCF_DONT_SWAP_OUT and terminal recovery returned 42.
partial_output_recheck.scheduler: TaskMessageSchedulingChecks returned 42; MessageScan, KeyScan, CharScan and FlushMessages do not switch tasks; explicit Yield and blocked MessageGet do.
partial_output_recheck.dead_task_heaps: Three UserText terminal/filter cycles including long input and error recovery passed. Every post-close snapshot reported zero live allocations owned by finished tasks. This does not detect allocations held by live tasks or global heaps; whole-system no-growth remains separate and unverified.
partial_output_recheck.whole_system_recheck: All UserText functional and repeated close checks passed, but aggregate data usage increased from 31411760 to 31412448 bytes with code bytes and allocation count unchanged; the no-growth check failed. This remains open.

graphical_recovery_recheck.initial_failure: The strengthened check found the bootstrap shell mistook Ctrl-Alt-C for its Ctrl-C escape and stopped the graphical terminal; serial recovery alone had masked that. A subsequent heap read faulted because the terminal pointer was no longer valid.
graphical_recovery_recheck.change: The keyboard byte ring records whether Alt was held when each byte was generated. The shell's Ctrl-C escape ignores Ctrl-Alt-C while the guest key-message path still receives the chord.
graphical_recovery_recheck.result: Three successive QEMU VirtIO DebugDemo runs accepted Ctrl-Alt-C. After each, the graphical terminal remained active and executed a fresh XTalk command. The live terminal heap rose as output accumulated; the test cannot isolate leaked allocations from document growth.
graphical_recovery_recheck.plain_ctrl_c_race: A further check found that guest polling could consume a plain Ctrl-C before the bootstrap shell saw it. The message reader now records that pending shell escape only for Ctrl-C without Alt when a GUI task owns input.
graphical_recovery_recheck.final_result: QEMU VirtIO and QEMU xHCI USB keyboard each passed three Ctrl-Alt-C interruptions followed by a new command in the still-running graphical terminal, then plain Ctrl-C stopped the graphical terminal and the serial shell returned 42. This does not establish live UTM or Pi input behavior or prove the growing live terminal heap has no leaks.

isolated_partial_output_cleanup.test: A live graphical terminal task creates an independent document, writes into it, catches Break when requested, deletes it and measures its own data heap. One normal run precedes three keyboard-interrupted runs.
isolated_partial_output_cleanup.negative_control: Unmodified DocPrintPartial retained [0, 32, 16, 16] bytes: the normal run retained zero and the interrupted runs retained temporary allocations. The test failed as intended.
isolated_partial_output_cleanup.change: The initial guarded source-bundle overlay retained the pinned output and conditional-yield logic, but released the scratch buffer and any document lock acquired by the function before rethrowing an exception during document processing. The original pinned source is unchanged. This check did not cover exceptions raised earlier by user_put_s callbacks; the later callback check below does.
isolated_partial_output_cleanup.result: QEMU normal completion and three Ctrl-Alt-C interruptions each retained zero bytes after deleting the independent document: [0, 0, 0, 0]. The separate document-flag test still passed. This does not settle aggregate UserText growth or validate live UTM/Pi.
isolated_partial_output_cleanup.follow_up: The conditional document-yield test, three DebugDemo Ctrl-Alt-C/graphical-recovery cycles with plain Ctrl-C shell escape, and three UserText terminal/filter cycles with no dead-task heap owners passed on the same kernel and source bundle. The UserText boot reported 111.9 seconds; the timing cause is not established. Pi desktop and diagnostic builds completed; neither has been tested on hardware.

callback_cleanup.test: A temporary document callback handles output, declines output, and throws an exception. The test checks normal callback behavior, exception propagation and live-task heap cleanup.
callback_cleanup.negative_control: Before extending the overlay, normal callback behavior passed but the throwing callback retained 16 bytes and the test failed.
callback_cleanup.result: The extended cleanup protects the callback as well; handled and declined output behaved as expected, the exception was propagated and caught, and no bytes were retained. The isolated keyboard-interruption cleanup check also passed all four runs with zero delta.
callback_cleanup.conditional_yield: The same bundle passed the DOCF_DONT_SWAP_OUT conditional-yield and terminal-recovery check. Pi desktop and diagnostic builds completed; live hardware behavior remains unverified.

next: Investigate shared/live-task memory and intermittent long-input timeout; verify Ctrl-Alt-D and live UTM/Pi behavior. MessageScan must not yield; pinned Sched.ZC is not the active scheduler.
